articles.headline: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) ruled out vs. Colts
articles.description: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels was ruled out of Sunday's game vs. the Colts, causing him to miss a second consecutive game because of a dislocated left elbow.
articles.body:
HERTFORDSHIRE, England - Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts, causing him to miss a second consecutive game because of a dislocated left elbow.

Marcus Mariota will make a second consecutive start. Meanwhile, the Commanders remain optimistic that Daniels will return soon -- possibly in Week 5 vs. the Giants.

"That's a huge positive step for us and for him," coach Dan Quinn said Friday of Daniels. "... Typical of him, he was more ready [to play this week] than you expect. That's just how he is."

The Commanders did receive good news Friday with the return of tight end Chig Okonkwo and linebacker Frankie Luvu. Both players missed the past two games with a hamstring and groin injury, respectively.

Daniels was a limited participant in practice all week, wearing a brace that leaves his non-throwing elbow slightly bent. He took part in individual drills, which included footwork portions as well as, at other times, needing to rotate his body and throw.

He said Thursday that he had no problems when doing basic quarterback moves that involve his left arm, whether taking snaps from center or handing off, and that he wasn't concerned with re-injuring his elbow, saying the brace is there to prevent that from happening.

Quinn said they want to assess Daniels after he gets a full practice in next week, with the decision to play coming from both a medical and performance standpoint.

Daniels dislocated his elbow for the second time in a year during a Week 2 loss at Dallas on the final play of the first half. His left foot was stepped on as he backed away from center; Daniels stumbled back and tried to brace his fall with his left arm.

He first dislocated the elbow last season in Week 9, causing him to miss four games. He reaggravated it upon his return and the Commanders decided to shut him down for the rest of the season.

Mariota completed 19 of 31 passes for 183 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks.

Luvu's return comes at a good time after the Commanders had lost two backup inside linebackers to injuries. Leo Chenal fractured his neck last week and is out for the season, while Jordan Magee was placed on injured reserve after the opener and won't be eligible to return until Week 6.

Because of the injuries, backup Kain Medrano played his first defensive snaps and returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown vs. Seattle.

Rookie Sonny Styles' start also helped lessen the impact of those losses. He was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week after recording an interception, a forced fumble and had multiple passes defensed vs. the Seahawks.

Okonkwo, who was signed to a three-year deal in the offseason with the hope of providing more explosive plays at tight end, caught two passes for 16 yards in the opener.

Running back Rachaad White, who has not practiced this week due to a shoulder injury, has not yet been ruled out vs. the Colts.

W

articles.headline: DraftKings DFS cheat sheet: Best values for Sunday's main slate
articles.description: Build a winning DFS lineup with our DraftKings NFL Week 4 cheat sheet identifying the players you want to spend up for, the teams to stack, the value picks to grab and the players you need to avoid.
articles.body:
Set a winning lineup for DraftKing's NFL Sunday Week 4 main slate by combining value picks in each roster slot and exploiting the best matchups, all within the confines of the salary cap. Every week, we evaluate all of your DraftKings options to identify the best values among the lower-priced options, as well as the matchups to play or avoid, so you can select the players who are worth their high price tags.

Value is determined by the number of DraftKings points you can expect for every dollar invested in putting that player in your lineup. A player may be an "Average" or even a "Good" value while also projected to outscore a player identified as a "great value," but when you consider the cap hit and the salary you can put towards other players, you may decide that the "Great" value outweighs that projection.

Players considered to be a "Great" value are those in the 90th percentile of projected value picks for the week. "Good" plays are in the 75th percentile or better. "Average" plays span the 25th to 74th percentiles, while "Shaky" plays are in the 10th-24th percentiles. "Poor" picks encompass single-digit percentiles. Only players projected to score 4 points or more are displayed.

Player salaries are drawn from DraftKings' main slate and are based on the ESPN player projections at the time of publication.

articles.headline: Drew Brees inducted into ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame
articles.description: Drew Brees was first to 5,000 career fantasy points and stands as the No. 2 scorer of all time.
articles.body:
Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

Presenting the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame , which honors the best players and acknowledges the most memorable moments since the advent of our game in 1995, the first year fantasy football was available on ESPN.com.

Take me to the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame 

Class of 2026 Week 4 Inductee: Drew Brees

5,188.92 fantasy points

80,358 passing yards, 573 passing TDs, 25 rushing TDs

Brees was one of fantasy football's most prolific quarterbacks. Entering 2026, his 5,188.92 fantasy points, 80,358 passing yards, 573 passing touchdowns and 25 games of at least 30 fantasy points are all second most, behind only fellow fantasy Hall of Famer Tom Brady in NFL history. The two duked it out for the lead in those four categories over a three-season span from 2018 to 2020, but it was Brees who was first to 5,000 fantasy points and 80,000 passing yards. Brees scored at least 250 fantasy points in 13 consecutive seasons (2006-18), joining Brady as the only players with at least that many, and was a top-five overall scorer in five of them (2008, 2011-13, 2016).

Brees will be inducted Sunday during "Fantasy Focus Countdown" (10 a.m. ET on ESPN2). Tune in each week through Week 16 as we reveal all 18 members of the inaugural class of the ESPN Fantasy Football Hall of Fame.

articles.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
articles.description: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
articles.body:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns.

This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season.

Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. 

Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald, who unretired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. 

As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory.

Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.  

But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982.

If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's. 

As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape

We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season.

Week 4 update

Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. 

Week 3 update

There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

Week 2 update

articles.headline: Raphinha set to be fit for Barcelona clashes with PSG and Real Madrid - source
articles.description: Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.
articles.body:
Raphinha will be fit for Barcelona's double header against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid later this month after tests revealed no major injury to his right thigh on Friday, a source told ESPN.

Raphinha, 29, was taken off at half time of Brazil's 4-2 win over Australia on Tuesday after feeling some discomfort in his thigh.

He was subsequently removed from the Brazil squad for Saturday's game against India and flew back to Barcelona, were he underwent tests on Friday.

A club source told ESPN those tests had confirmed Brazil's initial assessment, that Raphinha "has edema in the thigh rather than an injury."

The news comes as a major relief to Barça after alarm bells were set ringing on Tuesday when Raphinha was taken off.

The forward missed 25 games for club and country last season due to a hamstring problem in the same thigh and there were fears he had suffered a relapse.

Despite the good news, sources say Barça will manage the player's minutes with caution ahead of some massive games in October.

Barça, who have won all eight of their matches this season, return to action after the international break on Oct. 10 against Getafe.

- UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

- Transfer rumors, news: Several Premier League clubs eye Koundé move

In theory, Raphinha could feature in that game, but coach Hansi Flick will make a decision on his participation in the days before the fixture.

Barça then travel to Galatasaray and Real Betis before a huge week which sees them face PSG in the Champions League on Oct. 20 and Madrid in LaLiga on Oct. 25.

Raphinha has been a revelation for Barça so far this season, shining in a new role as the team's No.9 after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

He has netted 14 times in eight appearances, including back-to-back hat tricks in his last two club games.

articles.headline: Former Man City manager Roberto Mancini 'not concerned' about charges
articles.description: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
articles.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of 1.45 million pounds (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about 12 million pounds ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.

articles.headline: Trail Blazers fire new announcer over past inappropriate posts
articles.description: The Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.
articles.headlineJa: トレイルブレイザーズ、過去の不適切な投稿を理由に新アナウンサーを解雇
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズは実況アナウンサーとしてブレイデン・ベル氏を採用したものの、彼が10代の頃に行った一連の不適切なSNS投稿が明らかになったため、同日中に解雇しました。
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers hired then on the same day fired Braiden Bell as their play-by-play announcer after a series of inappropriate social media posts from when he was a teenager came to light.

"The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments," the team said in a social media statement Thursday announcing Bell's dismissal. "Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster."

Among the insensitive comments, as found by a reporter for KGW in Portland, were Bell saying he was "not racist" but "Asian people piss me off" and a number of misogynistic posts, including him shouting out "big girls" and "closet whores." The posts were reportedly made in 2012 and 2013, around the time that Bell was 15 years old.

Bell, 29, had been hired to call games after broadcasting for the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury and G League's Valley Suns over the past two years.

Both Bell and his agent did not respond to requests for comment from multiple outlets. The agent referred questions from KGW, made before the firing, to the Trail Blazers.

"We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City," the Trail Blazers said. "We strongly believe that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better."

Bell was set to replace longtime play-by-play announcer Kevin Calabro, who had held the role since 2016 but left in July after what he told The Oregonian was a "subprime" contract offer.

New Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon has made a number of cost-cutting moves that have come under scrutiny. Dundon also insisted over the summer that only public money should be used to pay for a $600 million makeover of the Trail Blazers' arena, the Moda Center.
